<thought>To propose a concise 2‑step synthesis, I will use commercially available building blocks:
1. 4‑Methoxyaniline (COc1ccc(cc1)N) – the aniline component of the final amide.
2. 5‑Amino‑1,2,4‑triazine‑3‑carboxylic acid (c1ncnc(N)n1C(=O)O) – provides the triazine core, the amide carbonyl, and the exocyclic NH that will be alkylated.
3. 4‑(Azetidin‑1‑yl)benzyl bromide (BrCc1ccc(CN2CC(F)C2)cc1) – introduces the benzyl‑azetidine side chain onto the triazine nitrogen.

Step 1 (SN2 alkylation, template ID 2002): the amine of the triazine acid attacks the benzylic bromide, giving the N‑benzyl‑substituted triazine acid.
Step 2 (Amide coupling, template ID 1001): the free aniline couples with the carboxylic acid of the alkylated triazine (via standard peptide‑coupling reagents) to afford the target molecule.

All three precursors are commercially available and, based on typical catalog prices, their combined cost is well below the $9 999 limit. The route uses only two synthetic steps, satisfying the ≤3‑step requirement.

Now I will present the retrosynthetic tree in the required JSON format.
